data.narrative:
Open Cosmos is a Growth-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 13 peers across the Space & Aerospace sector—five public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) trading at a median 24.6x P/S, and eight private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $50M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, yielding $60M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible: while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-tier) contained the three or more datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-Comp Anchoring similarly could not be applied due to the absence of revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), with a median of $60M. This narrow range reflects methodological constraint: reliance on a single applicable approach limits confidence. Key uncertainties include Open Cosmos' revenue scale relative to the 24.6x public median, the relevance of the private peer set's valuations to current market conditions, and whether the 1.2x step-up multiplier appropriately reflects company-specific progress metrics. Further analysis would benefit from revenue guidance or comparable transaction data within the narrow Growth-stage cohort.
